Ms Calic, do you know about the position of the Bosnian Serbs who claimed that they said that 65-70 per cent of the territory belonged to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have heard about that. I cannot identify any person that said this or any date or concrete event.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: But you are familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With what? I cannot follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: The position -- you said that you were familiar but you did not know the source from which you found out this information. If I reminded you that Radovan Karadzic said that any number of times on television, would I have refreshed your memory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute before you answer. You filed a document showing the areas to which the Serbs were laying a claim and the area to which the Croats were laying a claim. Would the area claimed by the Serbs amount to about 70 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult to say, because I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You filed a document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I actually cannot state it very clearly where the exact borders of this territory were. I was wondering whether or not to prepare a map where these claimed territories are marked, and then I refrained from doing so because there might have been also other territories and then we would have, as in this case, just discussed parts of maybe Konjic or municipalities, and then we would have started a discussion on the exact borders of these territories. So I prepared just to leave it like it is and it was a bigger part. It was a bigger part of Bosnia. This is sure, but I would also -- maybe I did not understand the question very well. I thought you were referring to Serbs coming from Konjic, and I am not aware that any Serb of Konjic did make such a declaration, and, of course, views among the Serbs are very different. This was not only a unified view but there were, of course, radicals and then there were moderates, Yugoslav-oriented and so on. It is very difficult to treat these people just as one unified homogeneous group which would accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Ms Calic, I was not thinking about the Konjic area. I thought that was pretty clear when I posed the question. I was referring to the territory of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I simply did not understand you very well because I am here all day. It is my concentration ... it is not I did not want to understand you. I really did try to understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: I will re-state the question. When you asked whether the Serbs held the position that some 65-70 per cent of the territory of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina belonged to them -- after you responded to this question, you expressed a certain confusion saying that you were not sure whether I referred to Konjic, to the Konjic municipality, but what I had in mind was the entire state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh yes. Is this a question?

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: That is a clarification, because you said that it was not clear to you. So I am expecting an answer if you had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What is the question? MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): The question is whether the Bosnian Serbs had aspirations on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the level of 65-70 per cent of the territory, in other words whether that ratio or that proportion of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina belonged to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is very clear. There were certain Serbs who had claims on 60 per cent, maybe even more, maybe even 70 or maybe even 80 per cent, but we cannot say that all the Serbs had this claim. There were different views and different propositions as for the future of Bosnia and as for the future of Yugoslavia. There was not one unified view among the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: I will clarify a little bit. Did the leadership of the Bosnian Serbs, starting with Radovan Karadzic, express such views in public that 65-70 per cent of the territory of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina belonged to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. That is what I wanted you to express your views on. Do you know that the Serbs proclaimed certain territories as exclusively Serbian based on an ethnic principle where they formed the majority, that is where their share of the total population was over 51 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I presented yesterday documents supporting this.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that the Bosnian Serbs also proclaimed as Serbian territories where they were in a minority at a percentage level below 50 in what they used to call the ownership principle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know this.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on to another block of questions, a different topic. Is it true that the armed forces in the former SFRY consisted of the regular JNA troops and the TO units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Did each republic have its own staff of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Were there also municipal staffs of the Territorial Defence, Ms Calic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: All commanders of the municipal staffs and the republic staffs of the Territorial Defence were the JNA officers; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Further, does that mean that the municipal staffs of the TO had their own arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had their own arms.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Naturally that included the territorial staffs as well, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: I will withdraw the question. Are you familiar what arms were involved? Was it light arms or heavy arms, including the launchers, etc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were different kind of arms, but I would prefer to pass these questions to the military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that in supplying of arms to the Territorial Defence municipalities took part; that is they participated in financing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: In other words those arms were the arms belonging to all the population living in different municipalities and the republics and the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, those arms were not exclusively the possession of one ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Including the Serbian people; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Ms Calic, are you familiar with the fact that I believe that there was a decision made in 1990 or some time before the aggression on Croatia that all arms were to be put under the control of the JNA and stored in the barracks of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Ms Calic, are you familiar with the fact that all republics followed this direction with the exception of Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: And that the same was done by the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of the Konjic municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say, but I assume that it was true in many parts. It was done in Bosnia. I personally cannot confirm or not confirm, but I assume that this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: You did not answer my question, Ms Calic. I did not ask about other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I asked directly about the Konjic municipality, about the arms belonging to the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I presume this must have been done. She has answered the question already. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): She said she did not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I do not know about this municipality. She says generally this was done but she assumes this must also have been done in Konjic. She has answered your question. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Were these arms stored in the barracks of the former JNA in Ljuta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that. I could not verify many witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Frankly, you do not go about answering questions you cannot authenticate. You cannot answer such questions. You do not know what has happened. You do not know what the position is. That is not your area. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Ms Calic, in your expert report do you mention assumptions as your own views on things and your own conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Assumptions as my own conclusions? I cannot understand this. Can you clarify? Can you tell me the passage.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: I will clarify. You said that you assumed that it was done in the Konjic municipality as well. My next question was: do you introduce assumptions into your expert opinion as conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't. I do not and in this case I can also not answer these kind of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: But, Ms Calic, I will remind you that in your expert report you stated the following -- this is your report of 3rd March, page 8, last three lines. Let me refresh your memory: "For example, the weapons for the TO for the municipalities of Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor were stored in the Ljuta barracks". A moment ago you said this was your assumption and this is contained in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can clarify this. I saw many documents saying exactly this, that the weapons of the TO were stored there but I have no evidence. I have not seen any documents saying when it exactly happened, and according to which order or to which law. So I cannot say the month or the day or the order. The exact circumstances I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: But do you have the information that these arms were stored in that Ljuta barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw several documents that weapons were stored there.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: I found what you just offered and that is contained in documents that you provided to us, and there is an exact data that there were 5,930 light arms with 2 combat packages that used to be in the possession of the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to the report by the JNA from 20th March 1992? You are referring to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document which was offered by you to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: With -- this is not a document that the defence has presented to you, but you presented to the defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I presented it myself. The same report says that the JNA was trying go to transfer these weapons to other areas. I do not know to which extent they were successful in doing so, and I cannot say how many weapons exactly were at a certain moment in Konjic. I included this as a document showing that there were weapons and that the JNA was also concerned and trying to transfer them.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Ms Calic, can I infer that you forgot about your own evidence when a moment ago you could not remember that the arms were stored in the Ljuta barracks, as stated in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not forget. I just understood the question in a different way. I understood it in relation with the mentioned orders by the JNA to store these or to transfer certain weapons to the JNA facilities, and as for Konjic, I have not seen any of such orders by the JNA telling the TO to transfer -- to bring these weapons exactly on a certain day. So maybe I misunderstood you. I did not forget my own documents.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ms Calic, but initially you said that you assumed that there were weapons belonging to the Territorial Defence in the Ljuta barracks, and after I refreshed your memory, and then I cited -- quoted the document number 52?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I obviously misunderstood your question. I apologise for this.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: I will move on. There is transcript. I think it is useless to continue with this polemic. Given that you stated before that before the start of hostilities in Croatia, the JNA was almost entirely purged of non-Serbs, that is that only the Serbs formed the officer corps, does that mean that the JNA in this way had full control over the entire armaments of the former JNA and the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand from the same report which you introduced that there were also other weapons around in Bosnia, and I understand from what international observers were saying that there were quite a lot of weapons which were not under the control of JNA but were under control of militia, paramilitaries and private persons.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: My question was not about those weapons. It was about the weapons belonging to the TO and the JNA, not about the arms that were acquired illegally, regardless of where it was acquired from. In other words, can you say whether JNA in this way had control and supervision over the arms belonging to the former JNA and the Territorial Defence. That is the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had control of maybe a bigger part of these weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did JNA arm the Muslim population, Ms Calic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they armed primarily the Serb population. I introduced a document to support this view.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the JNA arm the Croatian population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They armed volunteers. They might have been Croats, they might have been Muslims, but primarily there was arming of the Serb population. The reporting tells us volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your answer. Were they arming Croats to fight Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that they were arming Croats to fight Croats. I did say this report is about arming volunteers, and we know from this, as well as from other reports, that the JNA was arming primarily Serb volunteers. I cannot say whether or not they might have been also volunteers coming from other nationalities, Yugoslavs maybe also, Yugoslav-oriented Croats, Yugoslav-oriented Muslims. I cannot tell this.

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Ms Calic, in your written report of March 3rd, 1997 you said that during March and April of 1992 there were armed conflicts between the HVO and the TO, on the one hand, and the JNA and the Serb forces on the other hand. This is referring to the municipality of Konjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would ask you to use the last report, not the one which I corrected afterwards. Can you please use the one of 7th March?

utterances.speaker: MR BRACKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will check. I was working -- I was checking the reports of 3rd and 7th March where I spotted some contradictions, and where I did not think of doing so in such crucial things, but -- let me refresh your memory -- you stated this yesterday during examination-in-chief by the prosecutor, and I have that on page 61, and I can quote it in English, the way you said it yesterday: "should there be any conflicts between the reports of March 3rd and March 7th".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have just in front of me the report of 7th March and maybe I can find it easier if you just repeat the passage. I am sure I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I would like, your Honour, to clarify these things. There are not two reports. There is one final report of 7th March filed with the Trial Chamber and with the defence lawyers. To make it possible for them to prepare we served them with the first copy that arrived, but then Dr Calic sat down and made some minor correction, and the report introduced in this hearing to the Trial Chamber is the report of 7th March filed with all of you. So I would also ask Dr Calic -- ask the defence lawyer to stick to the final report, which one he knows it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually I did not see any need for this, because the witness has already said in evidence that there is just one, one report. She admitted there was one in which she made corrections and the corrections is the last one, which was made for 7th March. I do not see why you are bothering yourself going over it again. It was in answer to counsel's question where she said there is only one report. It is fairly difficult to understand how you proceed with that. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I am not trying to introduce both reports into this. I agree that there is only one report, dated March 7, but I will add that I used as a work copy the report of March 3rd, when I started preparing for this cross-examination. So my question refers to -- is based on the report of March 7th, the only one that is treated here as the report before this Chamber. Ms Calic, if you are tired, I have nothing as far as I am concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: She should be tired now and it is 5.30. The Trial Chamber will now rise. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I just wanted to propose and say that I have nothing against that we conclude for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: There will be no sitting tomorrow. We will sit again on Monday at 10 o'clock. The Trial Chamber will now rise.

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until Monday morning at 10 o'clock)
